title: Quickstart: align with new onboarding flow (first request → streaming → cost dashboard) + add activation troubleshooting
author: Ethan Wallace
body:
## Summary
This updates the Redwood Inference Quickstart to match the new lifecycle onboarding flow being used by the activation emails + in-console checklist:
1) Create an API key
2) Make a first successful request (copy/paste curl)
3) Enable streaming and confirm you see incremental tokens
4) View latency + token cost in the Console dashboard

It also adds a dedicated troubleshooting section for the most common activation blockers Support/CS have been seeing (auth confusion, wrong console path, streaming disconnects).

## Why
Growth is shipping a lifecycle experiments sprint and the email sequence + console nudges now deep-link into specific docs sections. Our existing quickstart:
- didn’t highlight streaming early (users thought it was “slow” because they waited for a full response)
- referenced the old Console navigation paths (causing 404s / wrong page for some users)
- didn’t have a single “if you’re stuck” page to link from email #3/#4

References:
- Linear: PM-413 (email sequence requirements), PM-414 (console nudges)
- Jira: SUP-2841 (email/docs links leading to wrong console path), SUP-2862 (API key permissions/confusion)

## What changed
- Rewrote Quickstart to be a step-by-step onboarding checklist with explicit “expected result” after each step.
- Added a streaming-first example (curl + SDK snippets) and a short section on common streaming pitfalls.
- Added a new “Cost & latency dashboard” section with updated Console nav + what to look for (tokens in/out, p50/p95 latency).
- Added a new troubleshooting page focused on activation blockers referenced by onboarding emails.
- Added/updated redirects for old Console/doc paths to reduce 404s from previously-sent links.

## Changed areas / files (high level)
- docs/quickstart/index.md
- docs/quickstart/first-request.md (new)
- docs/quickstart/streaming.md
- docs/console/cost-dashboard.md
- docs/troubleshooting/activation.md (new)
- docs/troubleshooting/http-errors.md (expanded)
- docs/_redirects (updated)
- docs/_sidebar.yml (updated nav)

## Notable copy decisions
- Kept claims conservative and developer-first (no unsubstantiated benchmark numbers). Where we reference performance, we link to the benchmarks hub page rather than quoting specific ms/$ values in the quickstart.
- Avoided embedding UTMs in the canonical docs URLs. Emails/ads should append UTMs at send-time; docs remain stable + cacheable.

## Troubleshooting page contents
The new docs/troubleshooting/activation.md is designed to be linkable from email and the console banners. Sections included:
- “I’m getting 401 Unauthorized” (missing/invalid key, wrong env var, copying ‘Bearer ’ incorrectly)
- “403 Forbidden / insufficient permissions” (project vs org confusion; key scope explanation; points to Console > API Keys)
- “404 / wrong Console page” (updated nav + redirects; where to find Projects/Routes)
- “429 Rate limited” (free-tier burst, backoff, where to see limits)
- “Streaming disconnects / no incremental tokens” (proxies buffering, missing -N in curl, SDK flush settings)
- “Model not found / invalid model” (model catalog names; region availability)
- “Still stuck?” (support link + what info to include: request_id, timestamp, SDK version)

## Testing
- `npm run build` (docs build)
- `npm run link-check`
- Manually verified the three deep links that will be used in email CTAs:
  - /quickstart (landing)
  - /quickstart/first-request
  - /troubleshooting/activation
- Verified redirects for old Console paths referenced in earlier drafts resolve without 404.

## Rollout / coordination
- This PR should merge before email v1 launch so CTAs don’t break.
- After merge: Tyler will update the email templates to point at the new canonical paths (UTMs applied in sending tool).

## Screenshots (text-only)
- Quickstart now includes callouts: “Expected: HTTP 200 and a JSON response containing `output_text`.”
- Streaming section includes: “Expected: tokens appear over ~1–2s, not all at once.”
- Cost dashboard section includes: “Expected: request shows up within ~1–2 minutes with tokens_in/tokens_out.”

## Checklist
- [x] Links are stable and redirect coverage added for known older paths
- [x] Copy reviewed for tone/claims
- [x] Troubleshooting page written to match common Support issues
- [x] Docs build + link check pass

---

### Review conversation

**Soojin Lee (PMM)**: Please avoid any specific latency/cost claims unless we can cite a canonical benchmark page.

**Ethan Wallace (author)**: Done — removed the “X% cheaper” line from the intro and replaced with a link to /benchmarks. Kept the rest as “monitor cost/latency in Console”.

**Ben Carter (Growth)**: Can we make the streaming step more explicit? We’re seeing drop-off between first request and “it feels fast”.

**Ethan Wallace**: Added an “Expected result” box + a note about `curl -N` and proxy buffering. Also moved streaming above the longer SDK examples.

**Marissa Cole (Product - Console)**: Console nav changed last week; please use “Console → Usage → Latency & Cost” naming and avoid “Metrics” (old label).

**Ethan Wallace**: Updated the nav text and added a small note: labels may vary by org role.

**Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops)**: Confirm we’re not hardcoding UTMs.

**Ethan Wallace**: Confirmed. Canonical links only; UTMs should be applied in Iterable/ads.

### CI
- docs-build: pass
- link-check: pass
- markdown-lint: pass

### Merge
Squash merged into `main` on 2025-01-24. Release note: Quickstart updated for onboarding flow + new activation troubleshooting page.
